Philosophe grec, père du scepticisme : s: Greek philosopher, father of scepticism: suspend judgement to find peace.
Penseur chinois des Han. Son Lunheng dém: Han Chinese thinker. His Lunheng took apart the superstitions of his time.
Franciscain anglais. Il défend l'expérie: English Franciscan. He championed experience as the judge of knowledge.
Savant anglais. À une foire, la moyenne: English scientist. At a fair, the average guess of an ox's weight came out almost exact.
Médecin et sociologue. Sa Psychologie de: Physician and sociologist. His Psychology of Crowds (1895) described the individual lost in the mass.
Psychologue américain. Ses expériences s: American psychologist. His line experiments showed the pressure of the group.
Psychologue américaine. Elle montre qu'o: American psychologist. She showed that false memories can be implanted.
Programmeur et consultant italien, créat: Italian programmer and consultant, creator of EventStorming. In January 2013 he stated the law that bears his name: refuting nonsense takes far more energy than producing it.
Mathématicien, philosophe et homme polit: French Enlightenment mathematician, philosopher and politician. In 1785, he showed that a voting group is more likely to be right the larger it is, provided each member has better than even odds of being right.
Psychologue anglais, pionnier de la psyc: English psychologist, a pioneer of the psychology of reasoning. He devised the 2-4-6 task in 1960 and the four-card selection task in 1966.
Psychologue américain, professeur à Corn: American psychologist, professor at Cornell then at the University of Michigan. In 1999, with Justin Kruger, he showed that the least skilled are the ones who most overrate their level.
Psychologue américain, alors étudiant de: American psychologist, then David Dunning's student at Cornell. Their 1999 study gave its name to the Dunning–Kruger effect. He later taught at New York University's Stern School of Business.
